findings.title: || 0 fallback violates Known Failure Pattern #13 and spec rule
findings.description: PlatoTab.tsx line 42 passes `aiJobApplicationSummaryId: (status === "succeeded" && aiSummary?.id) || 0` to `useAiJobApplicationSummary`. When no summary exists or status is not "succeeded", `aiSummary?.id` is undefined/falsy and the `|| 0` fabricates a real-looking ID of `0`. This is the exact antipattern documented in Known Failure Pattern #13 (core_critical_rules.md rule 10): the previous instance sent GET /ai_job_application_summaries/0 on every render. The `enabled: !!aiJobApplicationSummaryId && aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0` guard in useAiJobApplicationSummary.ts line 44 happens to suppress the network request for the value 0, but the fabrication itself is the violation — the spec and KFP #13 prohibit `|| 0` regardless of downstream guards. The correct call pattern is to pass `undefined` (or omit the field) so the enabled guard works on a semantically null value rather than a fabricated integer.
findings.fix: Replace `(status === "succeeded" && aiSummary?.id) || 0` with `status === "succeeded" ? aiSummary?.id : undefined` (or equivalent). The enabled guard `!!aiJobApplicationSummaryId` already handles undefined correctly — no network request fires.
